questions.prompt: Which adjective is correctly built from its noun?
questions.explanation: The noun sun is consonant plus vowel plus consonant, so the n is doubled before the y: sunny. Writing suny or fogy forgets that doubling, and rainny adds it where it is not needed, because rain has two vowels in the middle and gives rainy.

questions.prompt: The sky is clear and there is no cloud. Complete: "It ___ rain tomorrow."
questions.explanation: A clear sky with no cloud announces that the rain will not come, and the negative of the future is won't followed by a bare verb: It won't rain tomorrow. The word will alone says the opposite, will not to adds a word that never follows it, and doesn't will puts an auxiliary in front of will.

questions.prompt: Read: "In December the temperature is 9 degrees. In April it is 18 degrees." Which sentence is true?
questions.explanation: 9 degrees is less than 18 degrees, so December is the colder of the two months: December is colder than April. Saying that April is colder, or that December is warmer, reads the numbers the wrong way round, and colder that April writes that where the comparison needs than.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about the future is completely correct?

options.text: Next week he will goes camping.
Next week he wills go camping.
Next week he will to go camping.
Next week he will go camping.

questions.explanation: After will the verb stays bare, and will itself never changes, even with he: Next week he will go camping. The -s of he belongs to what happens every day, it never lands on will or on the verb that follows it, and no to comes between the two.

questions.prompt: Complete: "I love ___ butterflies in the field when it is ___."
questions.explanation: After love the activity takes the -ing form, so it is catching; and the weather needs the adjective, so it is sunny and not the noun sun. Only one answer gets both halves right at the same time.

questions.prompt: Read: "There is snow on the mountain and the wind is strong." Which answer to the question What's the weather like? is correct?
questions.explanation: The answer opens with It's and takes the adjectives, which are the nouns plus a y: It's snowy and windy. Saying It's snow and wind keeps the two nouns, It snowy and windy loses the verb, and It's snowing and winding uses -ing forms, which name actions and not the weather of a day.
